variants.headline: Assembly votes down government bill
variants.sub: The Assembly has rejected a bill put forward by the government.
variants.body:
A government bill has been voted down in the Colonial Assembly. The result concerns the proposal put to the vote; it should not be enlarged into an unreported change of government. In assessing {target}, readers should distinguish legislative defeat from a complete account of political authority.

A bill that has been rejected is not a new operating rule. Business readers should resist the temptation to treat the proposal as enacted, or the defeat as a promise about all future legislation. Commercial planning needs the actual legal position, with proposed changes distinguished from decisions that take effect.

We defend {target} against an easy adverse verdict. A parliamentary defeat does not by itself settle the merits of a political position, and a rejected proposal can still deserve a fair hearing. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.

variants.headline: A proposal meets its parliamentary limit
variants.sub: A proposed government bill has failed in the Assembly vote.
